research_population: Aggregate gender-labeled owner reports and one vendor-selected U.S. 25–34 female gaming-viewer panel; not individuals or all creators; separate 2025 Australian YouTube-watching child survey age 6–13 and UK cross-app child genre directional survey; neither is a creator population

comparison_gates.reason: No validated person-level or aggregate intersection across beauty, gaming, and other niche groups
Vendor classification not established as equivalent to signed-in owner reporting
Logged-out viewers and suppressed demographic cells are not characterized
Panel recruitment probabilities and coverage weights missing

safeguards: Do not infer gender, sex, politics, religion or sexuality of anyone from names, images, voices or comments.
An account reporting category is not proof of biological sex or personal identity.
An unavailable analytics cell is unknown, not zero.
Vendor 5% overlap is not a known denominator or deduplicated union; do not multiply by panel n.
Content formats and communities can overlap; no gender stereotype is an empirical population model.
Do not store person-level demographics, identifiers, OAuth tokens or private watch histories.
No Australian child genre-by-gender survey percentage identifies personal traits or overlaps, creator composition or an intersection between gaming and fashion viewers.
UK Ofcom cross-video-app directional gender findings and Australian YouTube-conditioned child genre shares are distinct frames; do not pool.

limitations: Within-group conditional percentages of Australian surveyed YouTube-watching children, not the fraction of each genre audience composed of boys or girls.
The source survey's overall N=1129 is not each gender's YouTube-watching respondent cell or the reported genre cell denominator.
The same participant may enjoy several genres; without joint response tables there is no specific gaming-and-fashion intersection numerator.
The survey's reported boy/girl categories do not establish biological sex, personal gender identity or a basis for assigning traits to any child.
Age 6–13 and Australian country scope exclude generalization to U.S. adult vendor panel, global platform users, creators or 2026 monetization.
No private or individual child audience profiles, video views, comment identifiers or respondent records are collected.
